title: What each family member has earned since January 2025
summary: Only one family member's 2025 income is itemised in a public filing: Melania Trump. The spouse section of Donald Trump's 2025 OGE report (released 30 June 2026) lists $10.71M from the 'Melania' film, $6,011,259 from NFTs and $521,161 from her memoir, all paid through MKT World LLC. For everyone else the record is mostly equity at paper value, set out in SEC filings: Eric Trump's American Bitcoin stake (68.4M pre-split shares, about $23M at the 13 Nov 2026 close, against roughly $600M+ near the September 2025 peak), the sons' Dominari, SPAC founder, GrabAGun, Unusual Machines and Kalshi shares, and press net-worth estimates (Forbes: Eric about $280M in April 2026, Don Jr. about $300M in December 2025 after about $500M in September 2025, Barron about $150M in October 2025, Kushner above $1B in September 2025). The same OGE report shows that 30% of DT Marks DEFI and DT Marks SC, the entities receiving the World Liberty and USD1 money, belongs to unnamed 'Trump Family Members', but no filing says how much any son or Barron received. Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners was scheduled, per a Senate Finance Committee letter, to collect $90M more in management fees from foreign investors between September 2024 and August 2026; actual receipts and his personal take are not public. The same report shows unnamed family members holding 20% limited-partner interests in many of the foreign licensing companies, which reported $54.5M of 2025 fees; no split by person is given. Salaries, board fees and advisory pay for the sons are almost entirely undisclosed. Kalshi ended Donald Trump Jr.'s advisory role by mutual agreement on 12 Nov 2026, citing his firm's investment in Polymarket.

sub_claims.statement: Melania Trump received about $17.2M of income in 2025 from her film, NFTs and memoir.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED (primary document read). Part 5 ('Spouse's Employment Assets & Income') of Donald Trump's 2025 OGE Form 278e lists MKT World LLC (Palm Beach), described as set up 'to enter into various agreements, including but not limited to appearance and speaking engagements and the sale of NFTs and other collectables, to receive net proceeds from the book "Melania", and the film "Melania"'. It reports net proceeds of $10,710,000 from a licence agreement with Designers Manager for the film, $6,011,259 from NFT and collectible sales, and $521,161 from the Skyhorse memoir, $17,242,420 in total. The same section shows MBWT LLC (Ljubljana real estate) with capital gains of $100,001-$1,000,000. No speaking income is itemised for 2025. For comparison, the 2024 report lists $216,710.74 in NFT licence fees under MKT World. These are net proceeds as reported on the form; they are not profit after tax.

sub_claims.statement: Amazon paid about $40M for the Melania film, most of it to the First Lady.
sub_claims.finding: The $40M licence price was reported by Puck and the WSJ in January 2025; Amazon confirmed the deal but not the price (C44). The WSJ reported her share at more than 70% (about $28M). Only $10.71M appears on the 2025 disclosure. The gap is unexplained: it may be timing, with the rest paid in 2026 or later and the two-part follow-up series due on 20 Nov 2026, or the WSJ share may be wrong. The 2026 disclosure, due in 2027, should show whether more was paid. The more-than-70% share is single-source (WSJ).

sub_claims.statement: Melania Trump received money from the $MELANIA meme coin.
sub_claims.finding: No filing shows $MELANIA coin proceeds to her. The 2025 report lists only NFT and collectible licence income ($6.01M). Bubblemaps reported in April 2025 that about $30M of tokens were moved from 'community' wallets and partly sold, and later cited about $10M of team-wallet sales. No source traces those proceeds to Melania Trump or MKT World. A class action over the token (Hurlock v. Kelsier Ventures) describes her as used as a 'prop' and does not name her as a defendant. The CAP tracker assigns the $6.01M to '$MELANIA coin and related digital ventures' by its own inference.

sub_claims.statement: Unnamed Trump family members own 30% of the entities that receive World Liberty and USD1 money.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED (primary document read). In both the 2024 and 2025 OGE reports, DT Marks Defi LLC (line 124 of the 2025 report) and DT Marks SC LLC (line 114) are owned 'DT Marks Defi/SC Member Corp: 1%, DTTM Operations LLC 69%, & Trump Family Members 30%'. DTTM Operations sits under the President's revocable trust. For 2025, DT Marks Defi reports $65,625,000 from the WLF Holdco equity sale and token-sale distributions itemised across lines 124.3-124.12 (CAP sums them to $526,810,321). DT Marks SC reports $196,875,000 from Stablecoin Holdco. The form does not name the family members or split the 30%. Whether these income amounts are entity-level totals or the President's share is not stated on the form. INFERRED (our arithmetic, asserted by no source): if they are entity-level, 30% is about $237M; if they are the President's 70% share (CAP's reading of the equity line), the family members' 30% would be about $338M. Neither figure is a documented payment to any named person.

sub_claims.statement: Unnamed Trump family members hold 20% of many of the foreign licensing companies that collected fees in 2025.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED (primary document read in full). In the 2025 OGE report, most new licensing LLCs are owned 'DTTM Operations LLC - Limited Partner - 79%; Trump Family Members - Limited Partner - 20%' plus a 1% member corporation (some hotel and golf manager LLCs use DJT Holdings in place of DTTM Operations). Twelve such entities reported 2025 fees: Doha $5,250,000; Dubai DG $10,361,458.68; KSA $9,243,574.15; Abu Dhabi $5,000,000; Al Raha Beach $5,000,000; Bucharest $5,000,000; Vietnam $5,000,000; Gurgaon 69 $3,637,775; Hyderabad, Noida 94, Pune Mundhwa and Philippines SV $1,500,000 each. That is $54.49M of the $63.06M of foreign fees (C98). Older licences such as Oman, the Damac Dubai golf deals, Istanbul and Worli are 99% DTTM Operations. The 2024 report already showed the same 20% split for Dubai DG, KSA and Vietnam. The form names no family member and gives no split. INFERRED (our arithmetic, asserted by no source): if the reported fees are entity totals and were distributed pro rata, 20% is about $10.9M for 2025. Forbes separately estimated that Don Jr. earned about $3.2M from new foreign licensing deals in 2024. This overlaps C98's licensing rows and C96's country rows; do not add.

sub_claims.statement: Eric Trump's American Bitcoin stake made him a paper billionaire, and has since lost most of its value.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED share count (SEC filings, seen as search excerpts). Schedule 13D/A amendments in late 2025 and the April 2026 proxy list Eric Trump with 68,432,664 shares (68,147,664 through his 2015 revocable trust plus 285,000 directly), before a 1-for-15 reverse split in July 2026. That is about 4.56M shares after the split. The stock closed at $5.07 on 13 Nov 2026 (market cap $369M). INFERRED values (our arithmetic on split-adjusted closes): about $637M at the 9 Sept 2025 high close, about $116M at end-2025, about $80M at end-April 2026 and about $23M on 13 Nov 2026. Bloomberg separately estimated a loss of more than $600M from the peak. The Dec 2025 13D/A put the stake at 7.4% of 927.6M shares. At the 3 Sept 2025 debut Forbes briefly valued him above $1B, then at about $750M (mid-Sept 2025), $400M (Dec 2025) and about $280M (28 Apr 2026, article read in full: Forbes says the venture took his fortune from about $190M to $280M). Eric said in Dec 2025 that he was holding all his shares. Hut 8's CEO said the brothers did not sell at the lockup expiry. No sale by Eric is documented. One outlet reports that his three-year advisory agreement carries no compensation (single-source). These are paper values; no cash is documented.

sub_claims.statement: Donald Trump Jr. holds an American Bitcoin stake of known size.
sub_claims.finding: Don Jr. is described as a shareholder (Hut 8 CEO, Dec 2025), and Reuters said the brothers together held nearly 20% at listing. The proxy's ownership table does not list him, which suggests a stake below 5%, and no filing gives his share count. Forbes (Dec 2025, read in full) estimates from SEC documents that he probably owns between 1% and 5%, which at the high end would have added about $80M to his net worth then. That is an estimate. His ABTC paper value cannot be computed from any filing.

sub_claims.statement: The Trump sons received Dominari shares and could sell them.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED (13G filings, via C39). Each brother received 250,000 advisory shares and bought about $1M in the Feb 2025 $3.47 placement, for 966,138 shares each (6.71%) as of 21 Feb 2025, plus 432,276 warrant shares each. In May 2025 an S-3 registered their shares for resale (Bloomberg: about $9.6M combined at the time). A circulating figure that Don Jr. 'sold 1,504,322 shares leaving 144,092' reads the S-3 resale table (shares offered and shares held afterwards, assuming all are sold) as an actual sale; MarketWatch corrected a report to that effect. Later Schedule 13G filings for Don Jr. (seen as search excerpts, not read in full) show 1,182,276 shares (5.23%) as of 22 May 2026, and 1,398,414 shares (5.77%) in a September 2026 filing that reports his exercise of 216,138 Series A warrants on 18 Aug 2026. His holding rose; no sale is documented. A ticker-tracking site lists Eric at the same 5.77% (single-source). INFERRED values (our arithmetic): at the end-2025 close of $4.95, 966,138 shares were worth about $4.8M, against a cash cost of about $1M. At the $0.78 close on 13 Nov 2026, Don Jr.'s 1,398,414 shares were worth about $1.1M. Separately, both brothers invested in Dominari's American Ventures vehicle; Bloomberg reports paper gains on microcaps but no per-person figures.

sub_claims.statement: The sons hold founder shares in the New America Acquisition I SPAC.
sub_claims.finding: Per Reuters, AP and Capital Brief (C27), Eric received 3M founder shares and Don Jr. 2M, worth about $30M and $20M on paper at the $10 IPO price. The value depends on the SPAC completing a merger, which had not been announced by Nov 2026, and on the later trading price. Founder shares typically cost a nominal sum. This is contingent paper value, not cash.

sub_claims.statement: Donald Trump Jr. is paid in equity for board and advisory roles (GrabAGun, Unusual Machines, PSQ, Kalshi, Polymarket).
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED that pay is mostly in stock. A Dow Jones report (Sept 2025) counted eight advisory roles, and CREW counts four board seats (PublicSquare/PSQ, GrabAGun, BlinkRx, Colombier III) and four advisory roles (Unusual Machines, Polymarket, Dominari, New America SPAC). GrabAGun: 300,000 shares per an SEC filing (a December 2024 consultant agreement), worth about $4M after the July 2025 debut slide (Bloomberg); a later Form 4 reportedly took his direct holding to 311,433 (search excerpt). INFERRED (our arithmetic): about $0.45M at the $1.46 close on 13 Nov 2026, if still held. A governance summary describes these as shares for one year of strategic consulting (single-source). Unusual Machines: 331,580 shares (200,000 for the advisory role plus 131,580 bought at $1.52 per unit), about $4M in Oct 2025 (FT). No sale is reported. INFERRED (our arithmetic): about $3.7M at the $11.28 close on 13 Nov 2026, if still held. PSQ: a proxy summary describes director pay as $300,000 of initial RSUs and $150,000 a year. His own grants were not confirmed (single-source summary). Kalshi: more than $300,000 of shares when he joined in Jan 2025 (FT, NYT); the role ended on 12 Nov 2026 (see next point), and Kalshi declined to tell the FT what happens to the stake. A June 2026 report puts the stake at about $6M on paper after valuation growth, while the FT says it has been heavily diluted (single-source estimate). Polymarket: his advisory pay is undisclosed. 1789 Capital's reported roughly $500M Polymarket position belongs to the firm, not to him. 1789 partnership and Executive Branch club: his economic share is undisclosed. No cash board fees for him have been found in any filing.

sub_claims.statement: Kalshi ended Donald Trump Jr.'s advisory contract in November 2026.
sub_claims.finding: Kalshi and Donald Trump Jr. ended his advisory role by what both sides call a mutual decision, reported on 12-13 Nov 2026 (Unchained, relaying CNBC, AP and the FT; 24/7 Wall St. via AOL). A Kalshi spokesperson said: 'We have mutually agreed to end Don's advisory role after his firm's significant investment in a competitor this past summer', referring to 1789 Capital's Polymarket investment, and said political considerations played no part. Per AP, talks began in August 2026; two people familiar with the matter told one outlet that some at Kalshi also worried about the new Democratic majorities in Congress. He keeps his Polymarket advisory role (CNBC). Kalshi declined to tell the FT whether he keeps his equity, which the FT says has been heavily diluted while Kalshi's valuation rose to about $40B. No figure for the stake's current value is documented.

sub_claims.statement: Barron Trump has earned tens of millions from World Liberty and is worth about $150M.
sub_claims.finding: Both figures are ESTIMATES, not disclosures. WLF lists Barron as a co-founder. Forbes estimated about $40M of token-sale proceeds (about $25M after tax) in mid-2025, and about $150M of net worth in Sept/Oct 2025, assuming he holds about 10% of the WLF value attributed to the family, with locked tokens heavily discounted. Forbes's method is to apportion the family's estimated WLF value by assumed ownership shares; Barron's stake has not been disclosed. The OGE report shows only that unnamed family members hold 30% of DT Marks DEFI. In Dec 2025 Forbes (read in full) set out a different working assumption: if each of the three co-founder sons held about 7% of the WLF economics, each would have roughly $80M of after-tax cash from token sales. That is an apportionment, not a disclosure. No newer Barron net-worth figure was found. His beverage company, Sollos, has no reported revenue.

sub_claims.statement: Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners has collected large management fees from Gulf sovereign funds.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED (Senate Finance Committee letter of 24 Sept 2024, read in full). Affinity had collected about $157.5M in management fees from foreign investors, $87M of it from Saudi Arabia's PIF. The fees are 1.25% a year on PIF's $2B commitment from June 2021 to August 2026, and 2% on about $1B from five other investors. Affinity was 'guaranteed to collect an additional $90 million' from foreign investors from then until August 2026, $50M of it from PIF. The letter calls Kushner, as sole owner, 'the biggest beneficiary'. INFERRED (our pro-rata arithmetic): roughly $70-80M of that $90M falls between Jan 2025 and Aug 2026. Actual receipts after Sept 2024 have not been published. Fees are firm revenue that pays operating costs, so they are not Kushner's personal income. A March 2026 letter from Wyden and Garcia repeats the $157M figure. Form ADV showed about $6.16B of regulatory AUM at end-2025 (C15).

sub_claims.statement: Kushner raised about $5B of new Gulf money in 2025-26.
sub_claims.finding: The NYT reported in March 2026 that he was seeking '$5 billion or more'. Axios said Affinity was not formally in market and had begun discussions with PIF under its first-look rights. Bloomberg-sourced coverage quoted Affinity's chief legal officer as saying the firm had reversed course and did not intend to take in new capital while Kushner volunteers for the government. A New Yorker profile (Dexter Filkins, autumn 2026) said he was 'discreetly raising another five billion dollars'. Kushner's public rebuttal says preliminary conversations about a possible future fund are not a raise. No closing has been documented.

sub_claims.statement: Kushner gained from the EA buyout and the Paramount bid.
sub_claims.finding: EA: Affinity is a minority investor in the $55B take-private that closed in Aug 2026 (C80). Its equity contribution and any fees or carry are not public, so no gain can be measured. Paramount: Affinity joined the financing of Paramount Skydance's hostile bid for Warner Bros. Discovery in Oct 2025 and withdrew on 16 Dec 2025, citing changed investment dynamics. Axios's sources said it never had a substantial stake. No gain is documented.

sub_claims.statement: Kushner became a billionaire on Forbes's estimate.
sub_claims.finding: ESTIMATE. Forbes added him to its billionaires in Sept 2025, putting his net worth above $1B, up from about $900M. A relay of Forbes's breakdown values his 100% stake in Affinity's management company at about $215M (up from $170M in Oct 2024) and attributes more than half his fortune to his roughly 20% Kushner Companies stake. That breakdown was seen only via secondary sources (single-source relay). Forbes values a management company from its fee stream, not from the fund's assets.

sub_claims.statement: Press net-worth estimates for the sons.
sub_claims.finding: ESTIMATES. Forbes: Don Jr. about $500M (Sept 2025), then about $300M (8 Dec 2025, from about $50M in Nov 2024; read in full); Eric about $400M (4 Dec 2025), then about $280M (28 Apr 2026; read in full). Forbes's Dec 2025 piece also estimated that Don Jr. received about $3.2M in 2024 from new foreign licensing deals and valued his share of the family licensing business at about $34M. Forbes builds these from public stakes at market price, private stakes at estimated value, and estimated after-tax cash from token sales, minus debt. Bloomberg's index tracks the family as a whole, excludes locked tokens, and does not publish per-son figures. Eric disputed Forbes's Dec 2025 valuation without offering an alternative. Net worth changes are not income and must not be added to cash rows.

sub_claims.statement: Eric Trump earned money from ALT5 Sigma, Metaplanet, the Trump Organization and his book.
sub_claims.finding: No amounts are public. ALT5: he was named a director in Aug 2025, changed to board observer after Nasdaq discussions, and by April 2026 no longer appeared on the leadership page. No pay or equity to him is disclosed. Metaplanet strategic adviser (March 2025): terms undisclosed. Trump Organization: he runs it with Don Jr., and salaries and distributions are private. 'Under Siege' (Threshold Editions/Simon & Schuster, 14 Oct 2025): the advance and royalties are undisclosed. As private citizens the sons file no financial disclosures.

sub_claims.statement: Ivanka Trump, Lara Trump, Tiffany Trump, the Boulos family, Kimberly Guilfoyle and Charles Kushner have documented earnings in the term.
sub_claims.finding: Little is documented. Ivanka: no 2025-26 income figure was found. A Forbes figure of about $100M circulates without a date, and her Albania resort plans with Kushner are pre-revenue (C45). Lara: Fox News hosts 'My View with Lara Trump' from Feb 2025, and her salary is undisclosed. Tiffany: nothing documented. Michael Boulos: the reported roughly $300,000 yacht finder's fee (NYT, single-source) dates from 2022, before the term (C66). Massad Boulos and Charles Kushner draw federal salaries as senior adviser and ambassador, and no individual amount was found. Kimberly Guilfoyle (ambassador to Greece until she resigned on 13 Oct 2026) reported $1.7M of 2024 income before taking office. The WSJ reported she asked donor Eric Deters in July 2025 to pay a $100,000 Amex bill. Deters says he did not pay, and her lawyers say any payment would have been for speaking and appearances and dispute the texts. No receipt is documented.

corrections: Claimed (C44): outlets split on whether the $10.71M film fee is Donald Trump's or Melania Trump's income. The record shows: the primary 2025 OGE report lists it in Part 5, 'Spouse's Employment Assets & Income', under MKT World LLC, alongside $6,011,259 of NFT proceeds and $521,161 from the memoir. It is her income reported on his form.

Claimed (C42, C04): DT Marks DEFI is a 'Trump-owned' entity. The record shows: the 2024 and 2025 OGE reports list it as 69% DTTM Operations (the President's trust structure), 1% DT Marks Defi Member Corp and 30% 'Trump Family Members'. DT Marks SC has the same split. So part of the World Liberty money accrues to unnamed relatives. CAP's memo describes the split as 70/30.
Claimed (C29): Forbes estimated Eric Trump at about $400M (Dec 2025). The record shows: that figure has been superseded. Forbes put him at about $280M on 28 Apr 2026.

Claimed (C29): Eric's American Bitcoin stake was worth about $160M (Dec 2025). The record shows: that was right for early December (about $166M at the 4 Dec 2025 close, our arithmetic). It fell to about $116M by the 31 Dec 2025 close and, on 68,432,664 pre-split shares after the July 2026 1-for-15 reverse split, to about $23M at the $5.07 close on 13 Nov 2026.
A circulating claim that Don Jr. 'sold 1,504,322 Dominari shares' misreads the May 2025 S-3 resale table. No sale is documented, which matches C39.

Claimed: the brothers 'own' about 20% of American Bitcoin. The record shows: that was the combined Trump-linked holders' stake at launch. Only Eric's stake appears in the proxy, and Don Jr.'s is undisclosed.

16 Nov 2026 (audit): Claimed (earlier version of this check): Kalshi's ending of Donald Trump Jr.'s advisory contract was unverified. The record shows: Kalshi confirmed a mutual end to the role on 12 Nov 2026, citing his firm's Polymarket investment.

16 Nov 2026 (audit): The foreign licensing income on the President's form is not his alone: unnamed family members hold 20% limited-partner interests in twelve licensing LLCs that reported $54.49M of 2025 fees.
denials_and_context: Eric Trump disputed Forbes's Dec 2025 valuation without giving his own figure, and said in Dec 2025 that he was holding all his American Bitcoin shares and was '100% committed'.

A Trump Jr. spokesperson says he 'does not engage with the federal government on behalf of any company he invests in or advises'. Kalshi said he advises on marketing, not regulation. Spokespeople for both sons call them 'passive' investors in the American Ventures deals.

Kushner calls the New Yorker's $5B account false. He says preliminary conversations about a possible future fund are not fundraising, and that the anonymous sources described conversations that 'never happened'. Affinity's counsel has said its arrangements are compliant. The White House says he is an unpaid volunteer, not a federal employee required to file.
Amazon says the Melania licence came out of a 'thorough and competitive' process and has denied any impropriety (C44). Melania Trump's office has not commented on the amounts.
Guilfoyle calls the Deters allegations 'false' and says she will 'vigorously defend' her name.

The White House says the President's businesses are run by his children through a trust and that no conflicts exist. The sons are private citizens and file no disclosures, so most of their pay and distributions are not public.
Context: income received during the presidency is not by itself income earned because of it. Several ventures (the memoir, Kalshi, Unusual Machines) began before Jan 2025.
Context: paper values are point-in-time and volatile. American Bitcoin fell more than 90% from its peak, and SPAC founder shares are worth nothing if no merger closes.

Kalshi says the end of Donald Trump Jr.'s advisory role was mutual, was driven by his firm's investment in a competitor, and had nothing to do with politics. Kalshi and Polymarket reject any suggestion that their links to the Trumps shaped regulation.
Jeff Bezos has said it is 'just not correct' to describe the Melania film deal as a way of buying influence (Variety).
Context: the 20% family interests in licensing companies are ownership stakes in firm revenue; the form does not show what, if anything, was distributed to any family member.
